title: Exploring Safety-Utility Trade-Offs in Personalized Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the variance in LLM safety (refusal rates on unsafe prompts) and utility (accuracy on general knowledge, math, and programming tasks) when the system prompt specifies the user's physical ability (e.g., physically disabled, able-bodied).
Measuring changes in LLM safety and utility performance when personalized with different user religious identities (e.g., Jewish, Christian, Atheist, Muslim, Hindu) via system prompts.
Assessing the variance in model safety responses and reasoning accuracy when explicitly provided with different racial user identities (e.g., African, Hispanic, Asian, Caucasian) in the prompt.
Comparing LLM performance on safety and utility benchmarks when personalized with various gender identities (e.g., man, woman, transgender man/woman, non-binary).

Evaluating utility and safety score fluctuations when the system prompt indicates the user's political affiliation (e.g., Democrat, Republican, Independent, or affiliations with political organizations).
Measuring how specifying the user's age demographic (e.g., minor, teenager, adult, senior citizen) in the system prompt impacts the model's safety constraints and utility accuracy.

Analyzing the impact of personalizing the model to different user sexualities (e.g., straight, gay, lesbian, bisexual, asexual) on its mathematical, programming, general knowledge, and safety evaluations.
Testing the variance in model safety and utility when personalized with distinct countries of origin or culturally specific names from different nations.
Evaluating changes in safety and utility performance when the user identity is specified as belonging to different professions (e.g., lawyer, doctor, teacher, engineer, janitor).
